assertions.statement: The Web build and macOS/Windows Tauri packages open the same light-theme zh-CN workbench.
Opening a source populates outline, editor, preview, and diagnostics from one saved source snapshot.
Dirty editor state disables validation and build until an explicit atomic save succeeds.
Template selection and diagnostics use existing template and validation contracts.
Build progress is ordered and successful completion reports the final DOCX path.
Validation, permission, cancellation, render, and finalize failures preserve prior valid files and expose recovery.
React components call typed transport adapters without duplicating compiler behavior or leaking React, Tauri, or HTTP framework dependencies into core modules.
Core CLI and package imports remain usable without Node.js, Rust, Tauri, or an HTTP server.
Archived prototype contract tests locate stable archived evidence after the source change is archived.
Controller and view-model tests run headlessly and cover all required workbench states.
Keyboard, focus, labels, contrast, responsive layout, and resize behavior satisfy the approved workbench contract in browser, macOS, and Windows runtimes.
Desktop workflows remain local and deterministic with external sockets blocked and no credentials; Web workflows use only the configured ThesisForge HTTP adapter.
